title: Trump to Speak at TSMC Arizona Expansion Groundbreaking on December 4
excerpt: The Phoenix event, which the White House says will create 10,000 jobs when the expansion is completed, comes days after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's reinstatement and a day after his scheduled Senate testimony.
body:
• President Donald Trump will deliver remarks on December 4 at the groundbreaking for the next phase of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company's site in Phoenix, Arizona, according to a White House official cited by USA Today.
  • The White House official said the expansion will create 10,000 jobs when completed. TSMC customers and business partners will attend; the White House did not say whether Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will be there.
  • The trip comes days after Nvidia's board reinstated Huang as CEO on November 23, a reversal Trump says he pushed for, and one day after Huang is scheduled to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3.
  • For readers holding Nvidia shares or working in the US chip supply chain, the two dates to watch are December 3, when lawmakers question Huang on national security and export controls, and December 4, when Trump speaks in Phoenix.

President Donald Trump will travel to Arizona next week to speak at the groundbreaking ceremony for the expansion of a semiconductor manufacturing facility in Phoenix, a White House official told USA Today. Trump will deliver remarks on December 4 at an event marking the next phase of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company's site in Phoenix.

TSMC supplies advanced semiconductor chips to customers including Nvidia. The Phoenix facility manufactures Nvidia's "Blackwell" chip, which is used to build the supercomputers that power artificial intelligence. Nvidia's announcement last year that the Phoenix facility was producing Blackwell chips marked the first time those key building blocks for AI supercomputers were manufactured in the United States, and Nvidia is among TSMC's largest customers.

A chip event shadowed by the Huang controversy

The Arizona trip continues Trump's efforts to boost an industry that has been central to his economic strategy, but it lands in the middle of the controversy surrounding Huang. Trump pushed Nvidia's board to reinstate Huang after he resigned on November 12 following revelations of extramarital relationships, including with a woman suspected of working as a spy for the Chinese government. Huang rejoined the company on November 23.

Nvidia's board said it is confident, after receiving input from US officials, that Huang's "reinstatement poses no national security risk." Asked on November 26 during an event at Mar-a-Lago how he can be sure Huang is not a national security threat, Trump said, "based on information and belief. I think he's absolutely fine." The president said he has not spoken to Huang since his reinstatement.

"I will tell you, the market feels very good about it. I think I did a great thing for our country and even for the world."

— President Donald Trump, on Huang's reinstatement

Congress gets its turn on December 3

Huang faces scrutiny in Congress, where he is scheduled to testify next week. Lawmakers are expected to question him about his relationship with the suspected Chinese spy and about national security questions, and members of both parties have raised concerns. According to USA Today's earlier reporting, Huang is scheduled to give public testimony to the Senate Banking Committee on December 3.

"The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," said Senator Elizabeth Warren, the top Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee. Trump, asked by the New York Post on November 24 about potentially pardoning Huang, said: "It's always an option, I guess, but I don't think it'll be necessary."

What it means for the market

Nvidia became the first $5 trillion company last year, but its stock price is down considerably in recent weeks, spiking after Huang's reinstatement was announced before continuing to dip, USA Today reported. The board's vote to reinstate Huang was unanimous, the company said in a November 23 release. What happens in Phoenix on December 4 — and whether Huang attends — will be read as a signal of how closely the administration intends to stand behind the chipmaker while Congress investigates.
